rows.query: How much money may a fully KYC-verified prepaid wallet hold at once under RBI rules? Is that a transaction ceiling?

claims.text: A fully KYC-verified prepaid wallet may hold up to Rs. 2,00,000 at any point of time.
This amount is a ceiling on the outstanding balance rather than a transaction limit for loading or spending.

quotes.quote: ## 9.2 Full-KYC PPIs - Banks and non-banks shall be permitted to issue such PPIs after completing KYC of the PPI holder (as indicated in paragraph 6); - The Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP), as detailed in Department of Regulation’s Master Direction on KYC dated February 25, 2016 (as amended from time to time), can be used to open full-KYC PPIs as well as to convert Small PPIs of paragraph 9.1 into full-KYC PPIs; - Such PPIs shall be reloadable in nature; - The amount outstanding shall not exceed Rs.2,00,000/- at any point of time; - The funds can be transferred ‘back to source account’ (payment source from where the PPI was loaded) or ‘own bank account of the PPI holder’ (duly verified by the PPI issuer). PPI issuer shall set the limits within this ceiling considering the risk profile of the PPI

Safeguards against money laundering provisions 6.1 The Know Your Customer (KYC) / Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Combating Financing of Terrorism (CFT) guidelines issued by the Department of Regulation (DoR), RBI, in “[Master Direction – Know Your Customer Direction, 2016](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=11566)”, as updated from time to time, shall apply mutatis mutandis to all the entities issuing PPIs. 6.2 Provisions of Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and Rules framed thereunder, as amended from time to time, shall be applicable to PPI issuer. 6.3 PPI issuer shall maintain a log of all the transactions undertaken using the PPIs for at least ten years. rows.query: Must a bank use a text-message OTP as its second factor, or can it offer other compliant ways to authenticate a payment?

claims.text: Banks are not mandated to use text-message OTPs exclusively; the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Directions, 2025 state that while SMS-based One Time Passwords have been primarily adopted, no specific factor was mandated for authentication.
The RBI Directions, 2025 allow banks to leverage technological advancements for implementing alternative authentication mechanisms beyond SMS-based OTPs.

Historically, NPCI documents for IMPS and RuPay indicated that OTP generation is a two-factor authentication process where customers could obtain OTPs via various means including mobile banking applications, phone banking, or entering MMID and M-PIN.
For international RuPay transactions, NPCI recommended that Issuer IAS systems build mechanisms to send OTPs to registered email IDs as well as mobile numbers.

quotes.quote: ## 1. Introduction All digital payment transactions in India are required to meet the norm of two factors of authentication. While no specific factor was mandated for authentication, the digital payments ecosystem has primarily adopted SMS-based One Time Password (OTP) as the additional factor. As announced in [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies dated February 08, 2024](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=57276), in order to enable the payments ecosystem to leverage the technological advancements for implementing alternative authentication mechanisms, it has been decided to publish Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as “Directions”). The directions provide the broad principles which shall be complied with by all the participants in the payment chain, while using a form of authentication. While these directions are applicable only to domestic transactions, in order to provide a similar level of safety for online international transactions undertaken using cards issued in India, the directions also incorporate necessary instructions for specific cross-border card transactions, in line with the [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies****dated February 07, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=59693). These directions are issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007 (Act 51 of 2007).

As announced in [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies dated February 08, 2024](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=57276), in order to enable the payments ecosystem to leverage the technological advancements for implementing alternative authentication mechanisms, it has been decided to publish Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as “Directions”). The directions provide the broad principles which shall be complied with by all the participants in the payment chain, while using a form of authentication. While these directions are applicable only to domestic transactions, in order to provide a similar level of safety for online international transactions undertaken using cards issued in India, the directions also incorporate necessary instructions for specific cross-border card transactions, in line with the [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies****dated February 07, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=59693). These directions are issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007 (Act 51 of 2007).

sources.text: NATIONAL PAYMENTS CORPORATION OFINDIA Circular: NPCI/2018-19/RuPay/032 20th December, 2018 To All Member Banks - RuPay Subject: OTP (One Time Password) SMS format for E-commerce transactions As per RBI mandate online transactions have to be processed with Two Factor Authentication (2FA). OTP validation is the second factor of authentication and it is delivered vide text message on customer's mobile phone by Issuer Authentication System (IAS). It is noteworthy, few Issuing Banks are sending OTP message without mentioning channel and mode of purchase, which gives opportunity to fraudsters for unfair practices. NPCI is working to incorporate "Merchant name" and "Transaction Amount" as part of Auth_Initiate API calls to IAS(1't API triggered to Issuing Bank) so that OTP message can display the name of merchant along with transaction amount. We will appropriately release the circular for making necessary readiness and certification at Bank's end for this purpose. claims.text: Banks are not mandated to use text-message OTPs exclusively; the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Directions, 2025 state that while SMS-based One Time Passwords have been primarily adopted, no specific factor was mandated for authentication.
The RBI Directions, 2025 allow banks to leverage technological advancements for implementing alternative authentication mechanisms beyond SMS-based OTPs.

Historically, NPCI documents for IMPS and RuPay indicated that OTP generation is a two-factor authentication process where customers could obtain OTPs via various means including mobile banking applications, phone banking, or entering MMID and M-PIN.
For international RuPay transactions, NPCI recommended that Issuer IAS systems build mechanisms to send OTPs to registered email IDs as well as mobile numbers.

sources.text: ## 1. Introduction All digital payment transactions in India are required to meet the norm of two factors of authentication. While no specific factor was mandated for authentication, the digital payments ecosystem has primarily adopted SMS-based One Time Password (OTP) as the additional factor. As announced in [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies dated February 08, 2024](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=57276), in order to enable the payments ecosystem to leverage the technological advancements for implementing alternative authentication mechanisms, it has been decided to publish Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as “Directions”). The directions provide the broad principles which shall be complied with by all the participants in the payment chain, while using a form of authentication. While these directions are applicable only to domestic transactions, in order to provide a similar level of safety for online international transactions undertaken using cards issued in India, the directions also incorporate necessary instructions for specific cross-border card transactions, in line with the [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies****dated February 07, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=59693). These directions are issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007 (Act 51 of 2007).

findings.reason: The answer claims banks are not required to use text-message OTPs and may offer other compliant ways, citing S4. However, S1.1 explicitly states 'Customer can get OTP using any of the following ways from the bank:' followed by a list that includes mobile banking apps (S8.1), phone banking (S11.1), and MMID/M-PIN (S12.1). While S4 says no specific factor was mandated, the older NPCI documents (S1, S3, S8, S9, S11, S12) present SMS as a primary or listed option alongside others, creating ambiguity on whether 'any' implies a mandatory choice from a restricted list or if banks can invent new factors. The answer blurs this distinction by asserting freedom to choose without clarifying if the 'following ways' in S1 are exhaustive or illustrative.

Recurring payments primarily authorized by a physical form that the customer had to fill, sign and submit. This was an operationally expensive and manual process, which took days to process. API based eNACH more commonly known as eMandate. Currently, E-mandate registration can be done through Internet banking or Debit Card based authentication. Additionally, now a new variant through Aadhaar based authentication is introduced. The registration here will be done through Aadhaar and OTP based authentication. Major advantages of eMandates: • Increase customer retention: One-time digital authentication allows you to auto-debit your customer’s bank account helping your customer enjoy uninterrupted service–in the longer run building customer loyalty and customer retention. sources.text: NPCI/UPI/OC-151A/2023-24 14th December, 2023 To, Members - Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam / Sir, **Enhancement of Limits for UPI AutoPay** UPI Autopay (referred to as e-mandate for recurring payments functionality) was launched on July 2020. With this facility, customers can now enable recurring e-mandate using any UPI Apps, for recurring payments such as mobile bills, electricity bills, EMI payments, entertainment/OTT subscriptions, insurance, mutual funds among others. A reference is invited to Circular RBI/2023-2024/88 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-882/02.14.003/2022-23 issued by Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dated 12th December 2023 with subject “Processing of e-mandates for recurring” whereby RBI has decided to increase the limit from ₹15,000/- to ₹1,00,000/- per transaction for the following categories: - (a) subscription to mutual funds, - (b) payment for insurance premium, and - (c) payments for credit card bills. In line with the aforementioned circular, NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC-151/2022-23 dated 23rd June 2022, is being revised. UPI AutoPay Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA) (viz. UPI PIN) limit has been relaxed from ₹15,000/- to ₹1,00,000/- for the Merchant Category Codes (MCC) mentioned in Annexure A with immediate effect. For the MCCs mentioned in Annexure A:

To further augment the UPI LITE user experience, Auto Top-up on UPI LITE is being introduced. With this new feature, the UPI LITE balance will automatically be reloaded by an amount chosen by the user, not exceeding UPI LITE balance limit, whenever the balance falls below a minimum limit set by them. This increases the convenience and adaptability of UPI LITE by automating the process of reloading funds. Additionally, users shall be provided with the option of revoking the Auto Top-up mandate at any point of time by the PSP/App. Since the balance resides with user’s bank and the UPI LITE can be deleted anytime with instant refund of UPI LITE balance to user's main bank account, the requirement of pre-debit notification (PDN), which is a usual mechanism for merchant mandate payments, has been dispensed

sources.text: RareRAT Rone Coen Lp NPCI/UPI/OC No. 205/2024-25 27" August 2024 To, AIl UPI Members Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Introduction of Auto Top-up on UPI LITE This is in reference to NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC No. 138/2021-22, dated 16" March 2022 and NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24, dated 31° August 2023, whereby guidelines to operationalize UPI LITE small value transactions have been introduced. UPI LITE enhances the user experience by allowing PIN less transactions under 2500 with a maximum UPI LITE balance limit of 2000 at any point of time. To further augment the UPI LITE user experience, Auto Top-up on UPI LITE is being introduced. With this new feature, the UPI LITE balance will automatically be reloaded by an amount chosen by the user, not exceeding UPI LITE balance limit, whenever the balance falls below a minimum limit set by them. This increases the convenience and adaptability of UPI LITE by automating the process of reloading funds. Additionally, users shall be provided with the option of revoking the Auto Top-up mandate at any point of time by the PSP/App. Since the balance resides with user’s bank and the UPI LITE can be deleted anytime with instant refund of UPI LITE balance to user's main bank account, the requirement of pre-debit notification (PDN), which is a usual mechanism for merchant mandate payments, has been dispensed

claims.text: Automatic top-up of FASTag or NCMC does not require an alert a day before the debit because it is explicitly exempted from the standard pre-debit notification requirement.

The RBI framework mandates that issuers send a pre-transaction notification at least 24 hours prior to actual charge or debit for e-mandates, but this rule does not apply to auto-replenishment of FASTag and NCMC balances.

The UPI implementation integrates these exemptions by allowing auto-replenishment of NETC FASTag (MCC 4784) and RuPay NCMC (MCC 7412) without the 24-hour pre-debit notification under the e-mandate framework.

All UPI remitter banks, Payer PSP Banks, and concerned ecosystem stakeholders must implement this exemption with immediate effect to ensure auto-replenishment is used only for the intended purposes of NETC FASTag and RuPay NCMC.

The exemption applies specifically to auto-replenishment done under the exception of Pre-Debit Notification as per RBI guidelines, ensuring that the mechanism is used only for these specific mobility cards.

quotes.quote: ## 9.2 Full-KYC PPIs - Banks and non-banks shall be permitted to issue such PPIs after completing KYC of the PPI holder (as indicated in paragraph 6); - The Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP), as detailed in Department of Regulation’s Master Direction on KYC dated February 25, 2016 (as amended from time to time), can be used to open full-KYC PPIs as well as to convert Small PPIs of paragraph 9.1 into full-KYC PPIs; - Such PPIs shall be reloadable in nature; - The amount outstanding shall not exceed Rs.2,00,000/- at any point of time; - The funds can be transferred ‘back to source account’ (payment source from where the PPI was loaded) or ‘own bank account of the PPI holder’ (duly verified by the PPI issuer). However, PPI issuer shall set the limits considering the risk profile of the PPI holders, other operational risks, etc.; - PPI issuer shall provide the facility of ‘pre-registered beneficiaries’ whereby the PPI holder can register the beneficiaries by providing their bank account details, details of PPIs issued by same issuer (or different issuer as and when permitted), etc.; - In case of such pre-registered beneficiaries, the funds transfer limit shall not exceed Rs.2,00,000/- per month per beneficiary. PPI issuer shall set the limits within this ceiling considering the risk profile of the PPI

UPI Lite (including refunds, etc.) will be processed online in the User’s bank account maintained in the bank’s core banking system. The upper limit of an UPI Lite payment transaction shall be ₹200/-.The total limit of UPI Lite balance for an “On-device wallet” shall be ₹2,000/- at any point of time. Replenishment of funds in UPI Lite shall only be allowed in online mode with additional factor authentication (AFA) or using UPI AutoPay which has been registered by the User in online mode with AFA.

sources.text: NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 31st August 2023 To All Member-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam/Sir, **Subject: Enhancement in UPI LITE transaction limit to ₹500** UPI LITE has been designed to play a vital role in reducing infrastructure load on the Core Banking System of the banks. rows.query: Can I apply the full-KYC prepaid-wallet balance ceiling to UPI LITE? Explain the differences in balance and single-payment limits.

claims.text: The full-KYC prepaid-wallet balance ceiling of Rs. 2,00,000/- does not apply to UPI Lite because UPI Lite is a distinct product with its own specific limits.
The total limit for UPI Lite balance is Rs. 5,000/- at any point in time under the latest enhancement, whereas full-KYC PPIs allow a balance of up to Rs. 2,00,000/-.
The single-payment limit for UPI Lite is Rs. 1,000/- per transaction under the latest enhancement, while full-KYC PPIs have a monthly transfer limit of Rs. 2,00,000/- per beneficiary.

sources.text: volumes. As an efficient strategy to process large-scale small value digital payments and based on the guidelines issued by RBI for enabling mobile devices to support offline payments vide its circular no. CO.DPSS.POLC.No. S1264/ 02-14-003/2021-2022 titled “Framework for facilitating small value digital payments in offline mode” dated 3rd January 2022, NPCI has designed the “UPI Lite – On-Device wallet” (“UPI Lite”) functionality for UPI user (User). In phase 1, UPI Lite will process transactions in near offline mode i.e. debit offline and credit online, and at a later point, UPI Lite will process transactions in complete offline mode i.e. debit and credit both offline. A User of UPI App will have the option to enable UPI Lite i.e. “On-Device wallet” on her/his UPI App. Once enabled, the User can allocate funds from her/his bank account to UPI Lite. Such funds shall reside with the User’s bank in an escrow / pool / designated account and such balance shall reside on-device on the common library (CL) of the User’s UPI App. At present, only debit from UPI Lite balance shall be permitted and all credits to UPI Lite (including refunds, etc.) will be processed online in the User’s bank account maintained in the bank’s core banking system. rows.query: Can full-KYC prepaid-wallet holders use third-party UPI apps? Reconcile the RBI PPI directions with the older NPCI issuer-onboarding circular, without assuming blanket supersession.

claims.text: Full-KYC PPI holders can use third-party UPI apps because the RBI Master Directions explicitly permit PPI issuers to facilitate discovery of their full-KYC PPIs on third-party UPI mobile applications.
When using third-party UPI applications, transactions from PPIs are authenticated using the UPI credentials rather than the existing wallet credentials used for issuer application transactions.

The older NPCI circular (OC 134) mandates that PPI holders shall be on-boarded for UPI by their own PPI issuer only and that the issuer shall only link its customer wallets to the handle issued to it.

The older NPCI circular (OC 134) also states that authentication shall be completed by the PPI holder as per existing wallet credentials, which appears to conflict with the newer RBI direction requiring UPI credentials for third-party app transactions.

The reconciliation shows that while the older NPCI circular required onboarding by the own issuer and authentication via existing wallet credentials, the newer RBI directions allow for third-party app discovery but mandate UPI credential authentication for those specific transactions.

flagged_claims.text: The newer RBI Master Directions (circular number RBI/DPSS/2021-22/82) supersede the older NPCI circular regarding the specific mechanism of authentication on third-party apps, as the RBI directions are the governing Master Directions referenced by the NPCI circular itself.

Deployment of money collected 12.1 To ensure timely settlement, the non-bank PPI issuer shall invest the money collected against issuance of PPIs only as provided herein. 12.2 For the schemes operated by banks, the outstanding balance shall be part of the ‘net demand and time liabilities’ for the purpose of maintenance of reserve requirements. This position will be computed on the basis of balances appearing in the books of the bank as on the date of reporting. 12.3 Non-bank PPI issuer is required to maintain the outstanding balance in an escrow account with any scheduled commercial bank. An additional escrow account may be maintained with a different scheduled commercial bank at the discretion of the PPI issuer. For the purpose of maintenance of escrow account, payment system operated by the non-bank PPI issuer for issuance of PPIs shall be deemed to be ‘designated payment system’ under Section 23A of the PSS Act. Non-bank PPI issuer that is member of Centralised Payment Systems operated by RBI shall maintain a Current Account with RBI. Maintenance of escrow balance shall be subject to the following conditions:- (i) In case there is a need to shift the escrow account from one bank to another, the same shall be effected in a time-bound manner without unduly impacting the payment cycle to merchants. sources.text: NPCI /UPI/OC No. 35 /2017-18 October 11, 2017 To, All Member Banks - Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Guidelines for positioning of UPI/BHIM logo as payment mode at merchant location (offline and online) Merchant websites, apps or any other channel normally have multiple payment options including UPI. It is critical to have proper display of the acceptance brand of BHIM/UPI to create network effect and eliminate any confusion due to multiple brand displays for the UPI acceptance. In consultation with the steering committee following has been decided:  In terms of placement of UPI/BHIM option at the merchant check-out, BHIM/UPI shall be placed prominently with priority & preferably above any other BHIM/UPI or UPI enabled container/aggregator payment options. Any BHIM/UPI user shall be able to make payment under this option, using either collect or intent mode.  If the consumer selects the BHIM/UPI payment, the transaction should proceed without any additional details/logins from the customer (unless additional details are taken even for generic debit/credit card flow as then this becomes a merchant decision for all payment options offered to its customers).  For the merchants not displaying different payment options at checkout (for e.g. cards, wallets) can continue to have either aggregator or container payment option, with the provision to service all UPI registered users (without any restriction).

claims.text: Full-KYC PPI holders can use third-party UPI apps because the RBI Master Directions explicitly permit PPI issuers to facilitate discovery of their full-KYC PPIs on third-party UPI mobile applications.
When using third-party UPI applications, transactions from PPIs are authenticated using the UPI credentials rather than the existing wallet credentials used for issuer application transactions.

The older NPCI circular (OC 134) mandates that PPI holders shall be on-boarded for UPI by their own PPI issuer only and that the issuer shall only link its customer wallets to the handle issued to it.

The older NPCI circular (OC 134) also states that authentication shall be completed by the PPI holder as per existing wallet credentials, which appears to conflict with the newer RBI direction requiring UPI credentials for third-party app transactions.

The reconciliation shows that while the older NPCI circular required onboarding by the own issuer and authentication via existing wallet credentials, the newer RBI directions allow for third-party app discovery but mandate UPI credential authentication for those specific transactions.

rows.query: Can full-KYC prepaid-wallet holders use third-party UPI apps? Reconcile the RBI PPI directions with the older NPCI issuer-onboarding circular, without assuming blanket supersession.

claims.text: Yes, holders of full-KYC PPIs may use third-party UPI applications to make payments.

The RBI Master Directions (RBI/DPSS/2021-22/82) explicitly permit a PPI issuer to facilitate the discovery of its full-KYC PPIs on third-party UPI mobile applications, which then enable such PPIs to be linked to their PSP handles.
When using third-party UPI applications, transactions from PPIs are authenticated using UPI credentials rather than the existing wallet credentials used on the issuer's own application.

The NPCI circular (OC No. 134) reiterates that PPI holders shall be on-boarded for UPI by their own PPI issuer only and that the issuer shall only link its customer wallets to the handle issued to it, which is consistent with allowing use of third-party apps where the issuer facilitates discovery.

The older NPCI circular (Circular 35) exempts third-party P2P-only apps from interoperable conditions compliance of servicing other UPI customers, but does not prohibit full-KYC PPI holders from using such apps for payments.

Deployment of money collected 12.1 To ensure timely settlement, the non-bank PPI issuer shall invest the money collected against issuance of PPIs only as provided herein. 12.2 For the schemes operated by banks, the outstanding balance shall be part of the ‘net demand and time liabilities’ for the purpose of maintenance of reserve requirements. This position will be computed on the basis of balances appearing in the books of the bank as on the date of reporting. 12.3 Non-bank PPI issuer is required to maintain the outstanding balance in an escrow account with any scheduled commercial bank. An additional escrow account may be maintained with a different scheduled commercial bank at the discretion of the PPI issuer. For the purpose of maintenance of escrow account, payment system operated by the non-bank PPI issuer for issuance of PPIs shall be deemed to be ‘designated payment system’ under Section 23A of the PSS Act. Non-bank PPI issuer that is member of Centralised Payment Systems operated by RBI shall maintain a Current Account with RBI. Maintenance of escrow balance shall be subject to the following conditions:- (i) In case there is a need to shift the escrow account from one bank to another, the same shall be effected in a time-bound manner without unduly impacting the payment cycle to merchants. It is critical to have proper display of the acceptance brand of BHIM/UPI to create network effect and eliminate any confusion due to multiple brand displays for the UPI acceptance. In consultation with the steering committee following has been decided:  In terms of placement of UPI/BHIM option at the merchant check-out, BHIM/UPI shall be placed prominently with priority & preferably above any other BHIM/UPI or UPI enabled container/aggregator payment options. Any BHIM/UPI user shall be able to make payment under this option, using either collect or intent mode.  If the consumer selects the BHIM/UPI payment, the transaction should proceed without any additional details/logins from the customer (unless additional details are taken even for generic debit/credit card flow as then this becomes a merchant decision for all payment options offered to its customers).  For the merchants not displaying different payment options at checkout (for e.g. cards, wallets) can continue to have either aggregator or container payment option, with the provision to service all UPI registered users (without any restriction).

claims.text: Yes, holders of full-KYC PPIs may use third-party UPI applications to make payments.

The RBI Master Directions (RBI/DPSS/2021-22/82) explicitly permit a PPI issuer to facilitate the discovery of its full-KYC PPIs on third-party UPI mobile applications, which then enable such PPIs to be linked to their PSP handles.
When using third-party UPI applications, transactions from PPIs are authenticated using UPI credentials rather than the existing wallet credentials used on the issuer's own application.

The NPCI circular (OC No. 134) reiterates that PPI holders shall be on-boarded for UPI by their own PPI issuer only and that the issuer shall only link its customer wallets to the handle issued to it, which is consistent with allowing use of third-party apps where the issuer facilitates discovery.

The older NPCI circular (Circular 35) exempts third-party P2P-only apps from interoperable conditions compliance of servicing other UPI customers, but does not prohibit full-KYC PPI holders from using such apps for payments.

findings.reason: The answer asserts that full-KYC PPI holders can use third-party UPI apps because the RBI Master Directions permit issuers to facilitate discovery on such apps (S1.2). However, NPCI Circular OC 134 (S2.2) explicitly states that 'PPI holders shall be on-boarded for UPI by their own PPI issuer only' and that the issuer shall 'only link its customer wallets to the handle issued to it.' While the answer attempts to reconcile this by claiming consistency, the requirement to onboard *only* via the own issuer creates a potential conflict with the ability of third-party apps to directly on-board or facilitate usage if the third party is not acting merely as a discovery channel under strict issuer control. The distinction between 'facilitating discovery' and 'on-boarding' is blurred in the answer's reconciliation, potentially obscuring whether third-party apps can independently enable these wallets or only display them after the issuer has completed the mandatory on-boarding.

rows.query: If a FASTag or NCMC automatic top-up does not need advance debit notice, can the issuer skip the message after the debit as well?

claims.text: The issuer may skip the post-debit message for FASTag or NCMC automatic top-ups because pre-transaction notification is explicitly exempted for these auto-replenishment e-mandates.
The exemption from pre-debit notification applies specifically to e-mandates registered to auto-replenish balances of FASTag and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC).

sources.text: ## Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators The safety and security of payment systems is a key objective of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). To ensure that the authorised non-bank Payment System Operators (PSOs) are resilient to existing and emerging information systems and cyber security risks, it was announced in the [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=53536) issued as part of [Monetary Policy Statement dated April 08, 2022](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=53537) that RBI will issue directions on Cyber Resilience and Payment Security Controls for Payment System Operators (PSOs).

records.quote: ## Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators The safety and security of payment systems is a key objective of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). To ensure that the authorised non-bank Payment System Operators (PSOs) are resilient to existing and emerging information systems and cyber security risks, it was announced in the [Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=53536) issued as part of [Monetary Policy Statement dated April 08, 2022](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=53537) that RBI will issue directions on Cyber Resilience and Payment Security Controls for Payment System Operators (PSOs).

records.quote: ## B. Authorised non-bank PSPs: - Authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (PSS Act) to set up and operate payment system; - Minimum net-worth prescribed by RBI as per certificate of authorisation or ₹25 crore, whichever is higher; - Incorporation in India under the Companies Act, 1956 / 2013. Entities not fulfilling this requirement shall empower their Indian subsidiary / associate to enter into valid agreements with RBI; - Implementation of centralised processing systems; - Adequate technical competence and system readiness including cyber resilience; - Compliance to instructions on storage of payment system data; and - Recommendation of the concerned regulatory / supervisory department. 2.2.2 The uniform access criteria at the time of application for decentralised payment systems is given below: - Minimum CRAR of 9% (as per the latest audited balance sheet); - Net NPAs below 5% (as per the latest audited balance sheet); - Availability of Core Banking Solution / centralised processing system at applicant’s end; and - Recommendation of the concerned regulatory / supervisory department. 2.2.3 The recommendations of the regulatory / supervisory department of the RBI will be obtained independently, and need not be furnished by the applicant entity at the time of submission of the application. 2.2.4 Continuation of banks / primary dealers / authorised non-bank

quotes.quote: NPCI/UPI/OC-226A/2026-27 — 03rd July 2026 To, All UPI Member Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications Dear Sir/Madam, **Subject: Enhancement of Transaction Limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI** Reference is drawn to NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC-226/2025-26 dated 07th October 2025, wherein On-Device Biometric Authentication (Fingerprint, Face, etc) was introduced as an additional option for authentication in lieu of UPI PIN. In view of increasing adoption in the ecosystem, it has been decided to revise the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication (fingerprint, face, etc.) in UPI is hereby enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026. Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications to ensure adequate customer communication regarding the updated limit. All existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable, and participants are required to ensure adherence. Yours faithfully, SD/- Sourabh Tomar Deputy Chief UPI Product

rows.query: For UPI mandate execution, explain how response codes 59 and K1 were treated before and after the deemed-debit addendum.

claims.text: Before the deemed-debit addendum (Circular OC-128 dated 14 December 2021), response codes 59 and K1 were treated as Deemed Debit transactions when declined by the Remitter Bank based on risk score, meaning settlement occurred by debiting the remitter bank and crediting the acquirer bank.

Before the deemed-debit addendum (Circular OC-128A), response codes 59 and K1 were treated as Deemed Debit under Circular OC-128; after the addendum, they are explicitly excluded from the Deemed Debit scope per Circular OC-128A.

rows.query: IPO and RBI Retail Direct share merchant category 6211. Does that mean they also share the same UPI purpose code?

claims.text: No, sharing the same Merchant Category Code (MCC) 6211 does not mean IPO and RBI Retail Direct share the same UPI purpose code.
For Initial Public Offering (IPO), the designated purpose code is 01, while for GSec through RBI Retail Direct Scheme (RDS), the designated purpose code is 25.

findings.reason: The answer states that IPO and RBI Retail Direct share MCC 6211 but have different UPI purpose codes (01 vs 25). However, the provided evidence does not explicitly confirm that they *share* the same MCC 6211 in a way that implies a conflict or distinction requiring clarification; rather, multiple excerpts independently assign MCC 6211 to both categories with distinct purpose codes.
